decisive_items: painless right testicular swelling of several weeks’ duration
Testicular ultrasound showed enlargement and inhomogeneity of the right testis and epididymis with ipsilateral hydrocele
An 18 FDG PET/CT showed intense uptake (SUVmax 25.5) in the right testis but no uptake in the adrenal glands
response.rationale: Testicular lymphoma best fits an 82-year-old man with painless testicular swelling, epididymal involvement, hydrocele, persistent symptoms after antibiotics, and intense testicular FDG uptake. The adrenal lesions are non-FDG-avid and nonfunctioning, so they are best regarded as incidental rather than metastatic or lymphomatous.

rejected.why: Accounts only for the adrenal enlargement and ignores the FDG-avid testicular mass; the adrenal lesion is nonfunctional and non-avid, so it is not the primary diagnosis.

A Leydig cell tumor could explain a testicular mass, but the patient’s age, epididymal involvement, hydrocele, and very high FDG avidity strongly favor lymphoma; Leydig cell tumors are less common at this age and typically cause hormonal symptoms.

The new adrenal lesions raise concern for metastasis, but absent adrenal FDG uptake and normal adrenal function argue against metastatic disease; the testicular findings are best explained by primary testicular lymphoma.
Primary adrenal lymphoma is unlikely because the adrenal lesions show no FDG uptake and the patient lacks adrenal insufficiency or B symptoms; it also does not explain the testicular mass.
